intro: The exact verbs of a recipe, pots and dishes, and how to praise a meal.
p.rallar.consejo: You grate cheese, carrot or bread. The «ll» sounds like a «y»: «rra-YAR».
p.picar.consejo: It is also said of insects: «me ha picado un mosquito».
p.trocear.consejo: It comes from «trozo». The pieces from «trocear» are bigger than those from «picar».
p.exprimir.consejo: You «exprimes» an orange or a lemon. The juice comes out under pressure.
p.rebozar.consejo: Croquettes are «rebozadas». Coating with breadcrumbs is «empanar».
p.dorar.consejo: It comes from «oro»: something «dorado» is gold-coloured. Onion and bread get «dorados».
p.cocer.consejo: The o changes: «cuezo», «cueces». Do not mix it up with «coser», done with a needle.
p.a fuego lento.consejo: The opposite is «a fuego fuerte» or «a fuego vivo». «Lento» means slow.
p.al vapor.consejo: Vegetables «al vapor» cook without going into the water. The v sounds like b.
p.olla.consejo: The «ll» sounds like «y»: «O-ya». An «olla a presión» cooks very fast.
p.cazuela.consejo: It is wider and lower than the «olla». Many are made of clay.
p.fuente.consejo: It is also where water flows out in a square. The context makes it clear.
p.abrelatas.consejo: It is the same in singular and plural: «un abrelatas», «dos abrelatas». It is masculine.
p.sabroso.consejo: It comes from «sabor». To say it more strongly: «riquísimo» or «delicioso».
b1.titulo: Verbs for the knife and verbs for the heat
b1.texto:
**Cutting.** **Trocear** an apple, **picar** garlic or onion (very small), **rallar** cheese, **exprimir** a lemon, **pelar** a potato.

**Applying heat.** **Calentar**, **hervir**, **cocer**, **freír**, **asar**, **guisar**. More precisely: **dorar** the onion, **rebozar** the fish (in flour and egg), **cocer al vapor**, **cocer a fuego lento**.

**Containers.** **La olla** is deep; **la cazuela**, wide and low; **la fuente** is for taking food to the table.

**Compound nouns.** Verb + plural: **el abrelatas**, **el sacacorchos**. They are masculine and do not change: **los abrelatas**.

**Praise.** **Está sabroso**, **está exquisito**, **para chuparse los dedos**.
b2.f0.texto: Chop the onion very finely, please.
b2.f1.texto: Do I put the onion in the pot or in the casserole dish?
b2.f2.texto: It is browned first in the casserole dish, over a low heat.
b2.f3.texto: How long is the rice left to cook?
b2.f4.texto: It is left to cook for twenty minutes, until the grain is tender.
b2.f5.texto: I squeeze half a lemon over the rice to give it flavour.
b2.f7.texto: Serve the rice in the dish and take it to the table.
b4.titulo: Three ways to give an instruction
b4.texto:
A recipe can say the same thing in three ways:

- **Infinitive**, the style of books: **Dorar la cebolla**.
- **Impersonal se**: **Se dora la cebolla**. If the noun is plural, so is the verb: **Se doran las cebollas**.
- **Imperative**, the style of someone speaking to you: **Dora la cebolla** (tú), **dore la cebolla** (usted).

**How long.** Use **dejar cocer** and **durante**: **se deja cocer durante veinte minutos**.

**Hasta que** takes the **subjunctive** when it talks about something that has not happened yet: **hasta que esté tierno**, **hasta que se dore**.
b4.e0.texto: Brown the onion over a low heat.
b4.e1.texto: The cheese is grated over the soup.
b4.e2.texto: Cook the lentils until they are tender.
b5.f0.texto: My grandmother's kitchen smells of golden onion and bay leaf.
b5.f1.texto: On the stove, a black pot murmurs slowly like a sleeping cat.
b5.f2.texto: She cuts a carrot into pieces and puts it in the casserole dish.
b5.f3.texto: The steam rises to the ceiling and fogs the panes of the window.
b5.f4.texto: I watch her from the door, my nose full of smells.
b5.f5.texto: When the lentils are tender, my grandmother serves them in a deep dish.
b5.f6.texto: The stew steams on the table and fills the room with a thick smell.
b5.f7.texto: Every spoonful tastes of home and of Sunday.
b5.f8.texto: My grandfather cuts a piece of bread and dips it in the hot broth.
b5.f9.texto: When they finish, nobody speaks, because silence is also a way of praising.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: exprimir is pressing to get the juice out.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Rallar is making shreds with a grater, not getting juice.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Trocear is cutting into pieces; the juice does not come out by itself.
b6.pregunta: What do you do to a lemon to get its juice?
b7.frase: Cuece el arroz hasta que ____ tierno.
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is indicative. If it has not happened yet, «hasta que» needs the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the rice is not tender yet, so the subjunctive is needed.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is an infinitive. After «hasta que» comes a conjugated verb.
b7.pregunta: Which form does «hasta que» need here?
b8.frase: Se pica la cebolla muy fina
b8.traduccion: The onion is chopped very finely
b9.o0.refuerzo: It is the infinitive of cookbooks; it does not talk to anyone.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is impersonal: it says what is done, it talks to no one.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: the imperative speaks directly to one person.
b9.pregunta: Which sentence gives an order to one person?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «over a low heat».
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the fuente is the big dish for serving.
b11.o1.refuerzo: The olla is for cooking, not for carrying to the table.
b11.o2.refuerzo: An abrelatas opens tins; it is not a container.
b11.pregunta: What do you carry the stew to the table in?
b12.o0.refuerzo: These nouns add nothing in the plural.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: it is masculine and does not change in the plural.
b12.o2.refuerzo: No: «abrelatas» is masculine, so it is «los».
p.grano.consejo: «grano» is masculine: «el grano». The «gr» starts the word strongly: GRA-no.
p.tierno.consejo: The «ie» diphthong is one sound: TYER-no. Compare «tierra», land.
p.exprimo.consejo: «exprimir» is to squeeze out juice. Here «exprimo» has «yo» as its subject.
p.darle.glosa: to give it to him/her (infinitive with «le»)
p.servid.consejo: In Spain, the plural command ends in «-d»: «servid». The «v» is pronounced «b».
p.llevadlo.consejo: «llevadlo» = «llevad» + «lo». The «ll» sounds like «y» in most of Spain.
p.ralla.consejo: «ralla» has the sound «ya» at the end: RA-ya. It is the verb «rallar», to grate.
p.cuece.consejo: «cuece» comes from «cocer», to cook in water. The «c» before «ue» sounds like «k».
p.estén.consejo: The accent on «estén» marks the stressed last syllable: es-TEN. It appears after «hasta que».
p.tiernas.consejo: «tiernas» agrees with the feminine noun «lentejas». Compare the masculine «tiernos».
p.laurel.consejo: «el laurel» is a masculine noun. The stress is at the end: lau-REL.
p.dormido.consejo: «dormido» comes from «dormir». Here it describes a cat, so it means «asleep».
p.trocea.consejo: «trocea» contains «trozo», a piece. Say the «o» and «e» as two separate vowels: tro-THE-a.
p.zanahoria.consejo: «zanahoria» is feminine: «la zanahoria». The «z» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.empaña.consejo: «empañar» is to cover with mist. The «ñ» sounds like «ny»: em-PA-nya.
p.olores.consejo: «olor» is masculine, so the plural is «olores». The «r» between vowels is soft: o-LO-res.
p.honda.consejo: «honda» is the feminine form of «hondo». The «h» is silent: ON-da.
p.guiso.consejo: «gui» is pronounced «gi»: GI-so. «guiso» is a masculine noun.
p.humea.consejo: The «h» is silent, and the two vowels «e» «a» are separate: U-me-a.
p.espeso.consejo: «espeso» describes something thick, like a stew. The «s» is clear: es-PE-so.
p.cucharada.consejo: «cucharada» comes from «cuchara», spoon, plus «-ada», the amount it holds.
p.domingo.consejo: «domingo» is masculine: «el domingo». Write the days of the week in lower case in Spanish.
p.moja.consejo: «mojar» is to wet or dip. The «j» sounds like a strong «h»: MO-ja.
p.caldo.consejo: «caldo» is masculine: «el caldo». The «l» is clear and the stress is on «KAL».
